Job Description

As our Pensions Writer, you'll combine genuine pensions expertise with strong editorial judgement to turn complex rules, choices and industry changes into clear, useful content for our customers. You'll have pensions and retirement planning at the heart of your work, while also covering the investment, personal finance and economic issues that shape people's financial futures. Across articles, guides, newsletters, podcasts and video, you'll help people understand their options, make informed decisions and build the confidence that's at the heart of Feel Good Investing.

What you'll do

  • Research, write and edit engaging pensions and retirement content for our website, app, newsletters, guides and other customer communications.
  • Turn complex subjects such as pension tax rules, retirement income, drawdown, annuities, the State Pension, auto-enrolment, contribution allowances and pension transfers into clear, accessible content.
  • Stay on top of pensions legislation, regulation, government policy and industry developments, identifying the changes and topics that matter to customers.
  • Write across related personal finance and investment subjects, including ISAs, tax, savings, markets, inflation and interest rates.
  • Bring your pensions expertise to different formats, developing ideas and content for articles, campaigns, podcasts, videos and webinars.
  • Work closely with editorial, marketing, PR, product, technical and compliance colleagues to make sure our content is accurate, balanced and engaging.
  • Use audience insight, search trends and performance data to understand what works and continually improve our content.

What you'll bring

  • Proven experience writing about pensions, retirement planning or long-term savings, with the pensions knowledge to write confidently and authoritatively for a broad audience.
  • Strong knowledge of the UK pensions landscape, including defined contribution pensions, SIPPs, workplace pensions, pension tax rules and retirement options.
  • The ability to make complex or technical subjects clear, accurate and engaging, supported by excellent writing, editing and proofreading skills.
  • Sound editorial judgement and an understanding of how accessible financial content needs to work within regulatory and compliance requirements.
  • An interest in personal finance, investing and the wider economy, and the confidence to work with subject matter experts to question and clarify technical detail where needed.
  • Your pensions writing experience could have been gained in journalism, financial services, a pension provider or investment platform, consultancy, an agency or another content-focused environment. What's important is your ability to write clearly and authoritatively about pensions for a broad audience.
  • Experience writing for retail investors or consumer finance audiences would be useful, as would knowledge of financial promotions and Consumer Duty.
  • Familiarity with SEO, digital publishing or content performance tools, or experience creating newsletters, guides, scripts, podcasts or video content, would be an advantage.

About AJ Bell

At AJ Bell, we believe investing should feel good. Whether you're looking for an ISA, pension or dealing account, whether you want to invest with the help of a financial adviser or do it yourself, we have easy-to-use solutions to suit people from all walks of life.

We're one of the UK's fastest-growing investment platform businesses, trusted by everyone from professional financial advisers to first-time investors.

Today, over 762,000customers trust us to manage more than £121.5billion of assets. By continually striving to make investing simpler and more accessible, we're helping more people take control of their financial futures.

We're proud to be recognised as a Great Place to Work for the past two years, building on six consecutive years as one of the UK's Best 100 Companies to Work For. It's recognition we're proud of and a reflection of the supportive and collaborative culture we strive to create for our people.

What we offer

  • 25 days holiday, increasing with service + buy/sell scheme + bank holidays
  • 6% Pension with matched contributions

  • Share schemes (including free shares and BAYE)

  • Travel and bike loan schemes
  • Employee Assistance Programme

Life at AJ Bell

  • Learning and development opportunities tailored to you
  • Casual dress code

Our ways of working

We offer hybrid working, with a minimum of 50% of your working time per month spent in the office.

For new starters, there’s an initial period of full-time office working to help you settle in and build relationships.

About us

We are a leading integrated media and marketing services company at the heart of a community of over 590,000 UK healthcare professionals. With more than 30 years of experience, we produce industry-leading content and experiences through our award-winning brands, publications, and events. We produce trusted, data-driven content that informs and inspires healthcare professionals across the UK and Europe. We are a Great Place to Work and UK's Best Workplaces for Women certified employer, offering a range of benefits including 28 days annual leave (rising to 30 days after 2 years) excluding bank holidays, private healthcare insurance, flexible working and more.

The Role

Our Community Data Administrator will be responsible for the quality, coverage, depth and development of the organisation's HCP community. The role will ensure we have a high-quality, accurate, comprehensive, current, relevant and growing audience that meets the needs of the business and our clients.

They will develop a detailed understanding of the organisation's HCP data and the wider addressable HCP market, identifying where we have strong coverage, where gaps exist and what actions we can take to address them. They will use first- and third-party data, market intelligence and behavioural and engagement data to understand the composition and health of our community and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

This is a highly analytical role for someone who loves working with data, numbers and solving problems. They will interrogate datasets, spot patterns and anomalies, assess data quality and freshness, identify gaps and translate findings into clear actions.

Working closely with teams across the organisation, they will help source and evaluate new data, improve HCP profiling and segmentation, strengthen our understanding of audience engagement and ensure our HCP community becomes increasingly accurate, complete, current and commercially valuable.

Location: Central London (Hybrid)

Reporting to: Digital Director

Expected start date: January 2027

Salary: £30,000 to £38,000 per annum, depending on experience

Key Responsibilities:

Data Quality & Governance

Take ownership of the overall health of the organisation's HCP database, including accuracy, completeness, recency, duplication, consistency, consent and compliance. Establish clear definitions and standards for data quality and regularly measure the database against them, including agreed definitions for active HCPs, inactive HCPs, dormant records, complete profiles and verified HCPs. Identify data quality issues and work with relevant teams to implement solutions and continually improve the reliability of our data.

HCP Coverage & Gap Analysis

Build a detailed understanding of the organisation's coverage of the HCP market and identify gaps by profession, specialty, geography, seniority and other relevant characteristics. Develop clear, data-led plans to address priority audience gaps and measure the impact of actions taken.

Data Enrichment

Identify opportunities to enhance existing HCP records with additional data points and attributes, improving the completeness and depth of our profiles. Determine which additional attributes would provide the greatest audience, editorial and commercial value and identify appropriate sources for obtaining them.

Data Freshness & Engagement

Assess how recently and frequently HCPs interact with the organisation across our brands, websites, newsletters, events, CPD platforms, surveys and other products. Develop and maintain an HCP engagement scoring methodology that combines behavioural signals across the business to provide a consistent view of audience engagement. Use engagement and recency data to understand the active audience within our overall community and identify opportunities to increase engagement.

Audience Re-engagement & Cleansing

Identify inactive, ageing, duplicate, incomplete or low-confidence records. Work with relevant teams to determine appropriate approaches for re-engagement, verification, consolidation, suppression or removal. Monitor the effectiveness of re-engagement and cleansing activity and use the findings to continually improve our approach.

Data Matching & Deduplication

Develop approaches for identifying duplicate HCP records and matching individuals across different the organisation datasets, platforms and data sources. Investigate conflicting information and establish appropriate rules for determining the most reliable and current information. Support the development of an increasingly consistent and accurate single view of each HCP across the organisation.

Segmentation & Audience Insight

Develop meaningful HCP segments based on profession, specialty, geography, seniority, demographics, behaviour, engagement, recency and other relevant characteristics. Analyse these segments to identify patterns, opportunities and changes in audience behaviour. Translate complex data into clear insights that can be understood and acted upon by teams across the business.

Data Acquisition & Gap Closure

Research and evaluate new first- and third-party data sources that could strengthen the organisation's HCP community. Develop data-led recommendations for acquiring or generating data to address identified audience gaps and measure whether those interventions successfully improve coverage.

The Administrative Assistant plays a key role in maintaining effective administrative processes, managing documentation and correspondence, coordinating office activities, and contributing to the delivery of a professional and high-quality service across the Firm.

  • Maintain a high standard of confidentiality and security in respect of client information, records, and Firm data.

  • Ensure reasonable care is taken at all times for the health, safety, and welfare of yourself and others, adhering to all Firm policies and procedures.
  • Assist with any other administrative duties and projects reasonably requested by the Supervisor, Management Board, or other authorised managers.

Key Skills Required:

  • Previous experience in an administrative, office support, or professional services environment would be desirable but is not essential.
  • This is an entry-level role and would suit candidates looking to develop a career in office administration.
  • Legal or law firm experience is not required for this position.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with colleagues at all levels.
  • A professional, proactive, and positive approach to work.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced office environment and remain calm under pressure.
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
  • Self-motivated with the ability to use initiative and meet deadlines.
  • Strong IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and the ability to accurately process and manage digital information and records.

The recruitment process will fully comply with GDPR and other applicable laws. Background checks including CRB / DBS checks will establish your eligibility to work in the UK and suitability to the role.

Graduate Sales Executive

Join our team at Sumitomo Corporation and build a commercial career with a global trading organisation in a varied graduate role spanning sales, business development, market analysis and digital projects. Successful applicants need a degree or equivalent qualification in business, finance, science or a relevant technical subject.

If you’ve also worked in the following roles, we’d also like to hear from you: Graduate Business Development Executive, Junior Sales Executive, Sales Development Representative, Sales Support Executive, Business Development Executive, Account Executive, Sales Coordinator, Graduate Account Executive, Commercial Graduate

JOB TYPE: Full-Time, Permanent

WORKING HOURS: 35 Hours per Week, Monday to Friday

This is an exciting opportunity to build commercial capability across sales, business development, operations, marketing, data analytics and digital projects. The Graduate Sales Executive will support new projects, tender bids and business growth while learning how the wider operation works.

The Graduate Sales Executive will gain broad commercial and operational exposure, supporting customer enquiries, market intelligence, sales systems, financial modelling and process improvement.

With training and supervision, the Graduate Sales Executive will contribute to project delivery, audit support, stock control and accurate commercial records while developing broad business understanding.

Sumitomo Corporation Europe Limited (SCEU), as part of Sumitomo Corporation, is one of the world’s largest integrated trading groups. Our purpose is simple yet powerful: enriching lives and the world. We put customers at the heart of everything we do while embracing our responsibility to society. Inclusion is key – everyone is welcome, and everyone is treated fairly and with respect.

With a global presence and expertise in a wide variety of industries, we offer candidates a continued career growth in a forward-thinking and innovative environment. We are driving significant sustainable energy projects in the UK, leading the way on climate change and energy. Join us and be part of something that truly matters.

We look forward to you joining SCEU, where you will build lasting relationships, develop your skillset and contribute to our 400-year history of success.


WHY JOIN US?

  • Stunning views of the River Thames from our newly refurbished London office space with excellent facilities and a welcoming atmosphere
  • Contribute to work that supports sustainability, innovation and global responsibility

Your duties as the Graduate Sales Executive include:

  • Tender and Sales Support: Support tender preparation and sales activity for oil and gas, geothermal and CCS customers
  • Customer Enquiries: Gather enquiries and record commercial and technical requirements under sales team guidance
  • Market Intelligence: Research customers, competitors, projects and industry developments and prepare market updates
  • Commercial Materials: Prepare quotations, sales documents, presentations and marketing materials with team input
  • CRM and Pipeline Administration: Maintain customer, enquiry, opportunity, quotation and pipeline records in Salesforce and other sales systems with training and supervision
  • Digital and Business Improvement: Support digital system implementation, continuous improvement, project cost and financial modelling and business process mapping
  • Systems and Audit Support: Complete SAP, SC Core and Salesforce transactional input, month-end checks, record keeping and JSOX audit support

ESSENTIAL

  • Degree or equivalent qualification in business, finance, science or a relevant technical subject

DESIRABLE

  • Work experience completed during study
  • Experience within a multicultural business environment
  • Experience using SAP or another ERP system
  • Experience working with AI systems
  • Basic office experience
  • Understanding of the energy or steel industries


BENEFITS

  • Hybrid working – 3 days working in the office in London per week with 2 days working from home
  • 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays

  • Free onsite gym with pool and classes
  • 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme
  • Training and development tailored to your goals

You will be supporting secondary-aged students, helping them access the curriculum and providing both academic and emotional support throughout the school day.
The school is looking for individuals who can use their initiative, get stuck in and understand what needs to be done without constantly relying on direction from the class teacher.

Your responsibilities will include:
* Supporting students with their academic learning across a range of subjects.
* Providing 1:1 and small-group support where required.
* Supporting students with additional learning needs and SEN.
* Offering emotional support and encouragement to help students overcome barriers to learning.
* Building positive, trusting relationships with students.
* Encouraging engagement, independence and confidence in the classroom.
* Working collaboratively with teaching staff to support student progress.
* Taking initiative and adapting your approach to meet individual needs.

Who Are We Looking For?
We are particularly keen to hear from graduates with degrees in:
* Psychology or Educational Psychology.
* Education or Education Studies.
* English or English Literature.
* Mathematics.
* Science or related scientific disciplines.

Previous experience working with children or young people is highly desirable. This could include:
* University placements within schools.
* Previous employment as a Teaching Assistant or Learning Support Assistant.
* Private tutoring or academic mentoring.
* Experience supporting students with SEN.
* Youth work, coaching or other roles involving young people.

The ideal candidate will:
* Be educated to degree level in one of the subjects outlined above.
* Have previous experience working with children or young people.
* Be confident supporting students both academically and emotionally.
* Have excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
* Be proactive, enthusiastic and able to use their own initiative.
* Have a hands-on approach and be happy to get stuck in.

* Have a genuine passion for education and supporting young people.

* Full-time, long-term work until July 2027.
* The opportunity to gain valuable experience in a mainstream secondary school.
* An excellent stepping stone for graduates considering a career in teaching, educational psychology, SEN or wider education.
* The chance to develop classroom experience and make a genuine difference to students' academic and personal development.
* The opportunity to work alongside an experienced teaching team.

Interviews Taking Place ASAP!
The school is looking to interview suitable candidates as soon as possible, so we are keen to speak with interested graduates who are available to start at short notice.

If you are a proactive graduate with a relevant degree, experience working with young people and a passion for education, Aspire People would love to hear from you!

We are recruiting a Community Engagement Officer on behalf of a respected professional membership organisation.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised, personable and proactive individual to join a busy membership and engagement team, supporting professional communities, committees, working groups and a varied programme of events and educational initiatives.

The successful candidate will enjoy building relationships, facilitating online communities and ensuring the smooth coordination and delivery of membership activities, webinars and events.

The Role

Reporting to the Head of Membership & Engagement, you will provide operational and administrative support across the organisation's committees, working groups, membership communities and programmes.

Working closely with colleagues and volunteer groups, your responsibilities will include:

  • Supporting and coordinating committees, working groups and membership communities, including meeting arrangements, agendas, minute-taking, correspondence and action tracking.
  • Managing and moderating online membership communities, welcoming new participants, encouraging discussion and ensuring content is appropriate and engaging.
  • Acting as a first point of contact for event and webinar enquiries, managing shared inboxes and responding to member and delegate queries.
  • Supporting the end-to-end administration and logistical delivery of webinars and events, including platform setup, speaker liaison, presentation management and live event support.
  • Managing post-event feedback surveys, CPD certificates and delegate communications.
  • Maintaining event calendars, trackers and relevant website information, ensuring details are accurate and up to date.
  • Providing administrative and logistical support for educational programmes, accreditation schemes and other membership initiatives.
  • Supporting grant administration, member surveys and other organisational projects.
  • Identifying opportunities to improve administrative processes, member communications and the overall experience for volunteers and members.
  • Supporting the organisation at conferences and events as required.

We are seeking an experienced administrator or membership professional with excellent organisational, communication and relationship management skills.

You will ideally have:

  • Experience in online community management or moderation, such as professional forums, membership platforms or online groups.
  • A proven background in administration, ideally within a membership, events, committee, community or programme support environment.
  • Strong customer service skills, including experience managing shared inboxes and responding to enquiries professionally and efficiently.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including accurate minute-taking, proofreading and correspondence.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage several priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • The confidence to build relationships with senior professionals, volunteers and a diverse membership community.
  • Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new digital systems quickly.
  • Basic experience updating website content through a CMS and supporting online event promotion.
  • An understanding of GDPR and good data management practices.

Experience of supporting committees and working groups, administering webinars or coordinating events would be advantageous. Experience within a professional body, learned society or membership organisation would also be beneficial.

Familiarity with platforms such as Discourse, Freshdesk, Typeform, Canva or Kentico would be useful, although experience with equivalent systems will be considered.

You will be a self-starter with a flexible and adaptable approach, able to manage a varied workload independently while working collaboratively with colleagues and volunteers.

You will be personable, enthusiastic and highly organised, with excellent communication skills and the confidence to identify opportunities to improve processes and member services.

This is a varied role offering the opportunity to make a real contribution to member engagement, community development and the delivery of a busy programme of professional activities.

This is a hybrid role, with 2 days a week based in their London office.

Starting salary – 35K plus excellent benefits.

Apply now for immediate consideration.

reed-57497681.jobDescription:
4Recruitment Services are seeking an experienced Anti-Social Behaviour (ASB) and Community Safety Officer for our client based in Brent.

The successful candidate will investigate complaints of anti-social behaviour, implement appropriate interventions and take enforcement action where necessary. You will work closely with residents, colleagues, the police, housing teams and other partner agencies to resolve complex cases, protect vulnerable victims and improve community safety.

The postholder will be based in the clients office in Brent. There is potential to work from home one day per week; however, this arrangement is subject to review.

Key Responsibilities

  • Investigate complaints of anti-social behaviour and implement appropriate measures to address the behaviour, including referrals to partner agencies and enforcement action.
  • Coordinate community safety projects in support of local priorities.
  • Risk assess vulnerable victims of anti-social behaviour and implement appropriate case management plans.
  • Investigate complex cases, gather evidence and prepare case files for legal proceedings, prosecutions, tribunals and civil penalties where appropriate.
  • Work collaboratively with partner agencies to develop effective solutions to persistent anti-social behaviour.
  • Chair or co-chair multi-agency problem-solving meetings and coordinate interventions for high-profile cases and local ASB hotspots.
  • Support victims and witnesses before, during and after court proceedings, providing evidence in court on behalf of the organisation where required.
  • Maintain accurate case records and prepare reports, statistics and briefings for senior managers, councillors, committees and partner agencies.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of anti-social behaviour strategies, action plans and preventative initiatives.
  • Provide specialist advice, guidance and support to colleagues, including Housing Officers, on the investigation and management of ASB cases.
  • Work with police, enforcement officers and other stakeholders to improve information sharing and coordinate enforcement activity.
  • Support resident engagement, raise awareness of community safety issues and contribute to improving satisfaction with ASB case handling.

Essential Requirements

  • Relevant ASB qualification or experience working in a community safety-related field.
  • Experience working in a multi-agency community safety environment.
  • Experience investigating anti-social behaviour and preparing and presenting cases for enforcement action.
  • Experience delivering community safety outcomes using project management methods.
  • Knowledge of crime and disorder legislation and anti-social behaviour legislation.
  • Knowledge of ASB enforcement powers, including Public Spaces Protection Orders, Community Protection Notices, Closure Orders, Criminal Behaviour Orders, agreements and Dispersal Orders.
  • Understanding of structured problem-solving approaches, such as SARA and situational crime prevention.
  • Knowledge of data protection, information governance and appropriate information-sharing procedures.
  • Understanding of interventions involving perpetrators of ASB, particularly young people and families.

Recruitment is done in line with safe recruitment practices. 4Recruitment Services is an equal opportunities employer.

Our Client

Are you passionate about supporting young people and helping them build a brighter, more stable future?

We are working in partnership with a social enterprise to recruit a motivated, compassionate and creative Young Persons Coach to join a truely unique service, focused on preventing homelessness amongst young people.


This opportunity is not necessarily about having previous experience in homelessness, housing or support work. Instead, someone with the right attitude, passion and motivation to make a genuine difference to the lives of young people is what we are looking for!

We are looking for someone who can think outside the box, bring fresh ideas and take a genuinely individual approach to understanding the young person they are supporting. Someone who is willing to go above and beyond, think creatively and find innovative ways to engage, empower and help young people overcome the challenges they face.

The role

As a Young Persons Coach you will work directly with young people who are at imminent or longer-term risk of homelessness, providing tailored, holistic support to help prevent them from reaching crisis point.

This is about much more than simply finding someone accommodation. You will take the time to understand each young person's individual circumstances, aspirations, strengths and barriers, developing personalised support plans that help them build the foundations for a more independent and sustainable future.


What are we looking for?

Above all, we are looking for someone who genuinely wants to make a difference.

You might already have experience working with young people, within housing, education, youth work, social care or the charity sector. Equally, you might be looking to take your first step into this type of work.

Previous experience is not necessarily essential. What matters most is your personality, approach and motivation.

We would love to speak to people who are:

  • Passionate about supporting young people and preventing homelessness.

  • Empathetic, approachable and able to build meaningful relationships.

  • Creative and innovative, with the ability to think outside the box when finding solutions.

  • Genuinely interested in understanding each young person's individual circumstances rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach.

  • Patient, resilient and committed to empowering others.

  • Confident communicators who can build relationships with young people and partner organisations.

  • Organised, proactive and able to take ownership of their work.

  • Able to recognise barriers young people may face and think creatively about how to overcome them.

Why apply?

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a unique and exciting project where you can have a real and lasting impact on the lives of young people.

You will have the opportunity to work in a genuinely person-centred way, helping young people recognise their potential, overcome challenges and build the confidence and skills to move towards independent living.

We are particularly keen to hear from people who have the passion and drive to make a difference, even if they don't have direct experience in the sector.

If you are someone who believes in people, enjoys finding solutions and wants to help young people build a future away from homelessness, we would love to hear from you!

We are a Social Enterprise that works with disabled people, providing specialist computer equipment, 1-1 teaching and have an in-house software development team.

Assistive Solutions are a Disability Confident Employer.

About the role:

As an Academic Support Worker at Assistive Solutions, you will provide tailored practical support to disabled students in higher education. You will help students access their learning environment and materials, taking a person-centred approach that respects their needs and encourages independence.

The role requires face-to-face availability on university campuses in East London. Some remote support may also be available, depending on students' agreed requirements.

Session Delivery:

  • Deliver support within each student's agreed allocation. Depending on their needs, this may include the following:
  • Transitional Support: Help students settle into university, become familiar with key locations and facilities, and build confidence navigating campus.
  • Practical Assistance: Support students with physical or sensory impairments to access study venues, carry books or equipment and locate resources.
  • Study Assistance: Help students search library catalogues, locate and collect resources, photocopy materials, and organise notes and study materials.
  • Note Taking: Produce clear, accurate and well-organised notes during lectures and seminars. Identify key information and provide notes promptly in an accessible format.

Build a supportive, professional relationship with each student and adapt your approach to their individual needs. Work within agreed boundaries; the role does not include completing assignments, proofreading or providing subject tuition.

Administration and Communication:

  • Use the Assistive App to log sessions and maintain accurate records, ensuring sign-off from both the student and support worker.
  • Submit any required session summaries and payment documentation in line with Assistive Solutions' procedures and deadlines.
  • Communicate promptly with students and the NMH team about availability, attendance, concerns or changes to support.
  • Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries. Follow safeguarding procedures and report concerns promptly through the agreed channels.

About you:

Essential:

  • A completed university degree and a good understanding of university-level study.
  • Availability to support students face to face on university campuses.
  • Excellent organisation and time management, with a reliable and flexible approach.
  • Clear, sensitive and professional communication, both verbally and in writing.
  • Good written English, including spelling, grammar and punctuation, and the ability to identify and record key information from lectures and seminars.
  • An understanding of disability awareness, confidentiality, professional boundaries and safeguarding.
  • Ability to work independently, maintain accurate records and communicate regularly with our team.
  • A person-centred approach that respects individual needs and encourages students' independence.
  • Willingness to complete our two training modules before delivering support: Safeguarding and Understanding Different Types of NMH Support.
  • Willingness to engage fully in onboarding, discuss support with our team, respond constructively to feedback and follow Assistive Solutions' agreed processes.
  • The right to work in the UK, with appropriate evidence provided before starting.
  • A current DBS certificate acceptable to Assistive Solutions, or willingness to obtain one through us at your own expense.

Beneficial:

  • Experience supporting disabled people or learners in an educational, community or support setting.
  • Experience supporting students in higher education.
  • Familiarity with Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA), NMH support roles and inclusive practices.
  • Experience supporting neurodivergent students, including those with autism or ADHD.

Additional Information:

We value people who are warm, approachable and willing to learn. We welcome the experience you bring and expect everyone to communicate openly, participate in onboarding and adapt their support to each student.

Appointment is subject to satisfactory pre-engagement checks. Please let us know if you need adjustments during recruitment or application information in an accessible format.

reed-57547148.jobDescription:
Location: Greater Manchester

Are you passionate about creating places that bring people together? Do you enjoy delivering events, building relationships and finding ways to improve the visitor experience?

Cobalt is recruiting a Placemaking Manager to join the management team of a shopping centre in Greater Manchester. This opportunity offers the chance to shape how visitors, occupiers and the wider community engage with a retail destination, delivering initiatives that make a difference to the people who use it.

The organisation

Our client is an established property management business responsible for managing commercial destinations across the UK.

With a focus on customer experience, community engagement and placemaking, the organisation works to create destinations where people want to visit, spend time and connect.

The Placemaking Manager will work alongside property management professionals and specialist placemaking teams, contributing to initiatives that enhance the shopping centre's identity, support its occupiers and strengthen its relationship with the local community.

The role and responsibilities

Reporting to the Centre Manager, the Placemaking Manager will take responsibility for co-ordinating and delivering a programme of events, campaigns and engagement initiatives across the shopping centre.

The role combines creativity, stakeholder engagement and project delivery, offering the opportunity to influence the visitor experience and contribute to the centre's ongoing development.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Supporting the development and delivery of placemaking strategies, events and community engagement programmes.
  • Planning and managing events from concept through to delivery, including budgets, suppliers and operational requirements.
  • Building relationships with retailers, occupiers, community groups and stakeholders to encourage collaboration and participation.
  • Creating content for marketing campaigns, digital platforms, newsletters and on-site communications.
  • Managing communication plans to promote centre activities and encourage visitor engagement.
  • Gathering visitor feedback, analysing performance data and identifying opportunities to improve the customer experience.
  • Working with centre management and property management teams to ensure events comply with health and safety requirements, including relevant licences and risk assessments.
  • Supporting reporting, customer surveys and award submissions that demonstrate the centre's contribution to the local community.

The skills needed

The successful Placemaking Manager will bring experience in event delivery, community engagement or destination marketing, alongside the ability to manage projects and build relationships.

We are particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate:

  • Experience planning and delivering events, campaigns or community engagement initiatives.
  • An ability to build relationships with stakeholders, occupiers, suppliers and community organisations.
  • Written communication skills, including creating marketing content, reports and presentations.
  • Working knowledge of digital marketing channels, social media platforms and Microsoft Office.
  • Organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver projects to deadlines.
  • An understanding of health and safety requirements associated with events and public spaces.
  • A willingness to obtain IOSH Managing Safely certification if not already qualified.

Experience within shopping centres, retail destinations or other commercial environments would be advantageous, although candidates from other relevant backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Interested in finding out more?

If you're looking for a Placemaking Manager opportunity where you can bring ideas to life, build community connections and contribute to the success of a retail destination, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today to be considered for this permanent opportunity. Applications are being reviewed as they are received.

Due to the volume of applications received, if you don't hear back from us, please assume your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

If you require any adjustments or additional support during the recruitment process for any reason whatsoever, please let your Cobalt consultant know.

We’re looking for a Communications & Events Partner to take the lead on planning and delivering some of Stonewater’s key corporate events and colleague engagement activities.

From our annual Company Day and One Connect sessions to leadership activities and wider corporate events, you’ll create engaging experiences that bring colleagues together, strengthen connections and help bring our organisational priorities to life.

This is a varied, hands-on role where you’ll take an event from the initial idea right through to delivery and evaluation. One day you could be shaping an agenda and working with senior leaders on content, and the next you might be coordinating suppliers, managing event technology or making sure everything is ready for the big day.

What you’ll be doing

  • Lead the planning and delivery of corporate events, taking ownership from concept through to evaluation.

  • Use digital and audience engagement tools to make our events accessible, professional and engaging.
  • Gather feedback and evaluate our events to continually improve the experience and demonstrate value.

You’ll have experience of event management, with the confidence to manage events of varying sizes and complexity and keep multiple priorities moving at once. You’ll need to be comfortable working independently and taking ownership, while knowing when to involve others.

Please note: Travel is an important part of the role, with events taking place across Stonewater’s national geography. You’ll therefore need a UK driving licence with business insurance and be happy to travel regularly as part of the role.

If you’re an organised, creative events professional who enjoys bringing people together and wants the opportunity to shape engaging experiences across a national organisation, we’d love to hear from you.

Location: Northenden, M22 4HH

Salary: Up to £28,000 per annum, dependent on experience

Job type: Full time, Permanent

Established in 2000, Express Solicitors is an award-winning, no win no fee law firm specialising exclusively in personal injury claims. Headquartered in Manchester, we support clients nationwide across all areas of personal injury, including employers' liability, serious injury, clinical negligence, occupiers' and public liability, road traffic accidents and industrial disease.

About The Role:

You will play key role as an experienced Legal Secretary supporting the Costs Department in servicing the costs needs of the business. You will be required to work independently servicing volume instructions from a digital dictation platform, this will include the creation of letters, witness statements, bundling of exhibits, file notes and other court documents, including court bundles.

Many of the documents and communications required will be prepared in digital format using complimentary software. Some paper documents, for postal delivery, remain necessary.

Whilst this is a busy role, it is varied and rewarding. In addition to typing and file management, you will assist with consulting with clients, third parties and the Court regularly by telephone, assisting with printing jobs and from time to time may be required to organise meetings and conferences.

You will join a team of experienced assistants, and secretaries who will provide you with training and support as you transition into the role.

Responsibilities:

  • Providing comprehensive secretarial and administrative support to Partners, Associates, Costs Lawyers, Costs Negotiators, and other members of the Costs Team.
  • Preparing, formatting, proofreading, and amending legal costs documents, preparing digital and paper bundles, correspondence, and court forms.
  • Managing diaries, arranging meetings and appointments.
  • Opening and closing client files in accordance with firm procedures and regulatory requirements.
  • Liaising with clients, solicitors, barristers, court staff, and external stakeholders in a professional manner.
  • Handling emails and telephone enquiries, ensuring matters are directed appropriately and dealt with promptly.
  • Assisting with the preparation and filing of court documents, including electronic filing where required.
  • Maintaining accurate records and ensuring all case management systems and databases are updated.
  • Organising and preparing bundles, exhibits, and supporting documentation for hearings, assessments, and negotiations.
  • Monitoring key dates, court deadlines, and limitation periods.
  • Audio typing of legal documents, correspondence and reports.
  • Assisting with billing administration, file reviews, and matter management processes as required.
  • Requesting and collating documents, records, invoices, and supporting evidence for costs claims and assessments.
  • Ensuring compliance with firm policies, confidentiality requirements, data protection legislation, and court rules.
  • Providing general administrative support including document scanning, photocopying, filing, archiving, and document management.
  • Supporting the team with ad hoc projects and administrative tasks to ensure the efficient operation of our Legal Costs department.

Person Specification:

  • Proven experience as a Legal Secretary in a busy team is essential
  • Excellent written English skills, with strong spelling, punctuation, and grammar
  • High level of IT literacy and confidence using modern office systems
  • Outstanding client care skills, with a professional and friendly telephone manner
  • Exceptional accuracy and attention to detail
  • Ability to prioritise workload effectively and thrive in a fast-paced environment
  • Previous experience using the Proclaim case management system is desirable but not essential
  • Advanced word processing and audio typing skills
  • Audio typing speed of 65+ words per minute
  • Experience using digital dictation software, ideally Diktamen, would be advantageous

Salary & Hours

  • Our standard working hours are 8:30am to 5:30pm Monday-Thursday and 8:30am to 5pm Friday.

Benefits:

  • 23 Days Holiday - Rising to 26 days, plus bank/public holidays.

reed-57586427.jobDescription:
Be a hero to a young person in care!

Are you looking for a meaningful, long-term volunteering role where you can make a positive difference in a young person’s life?

If yes, we have the perfect opportunity for you!

We’re seeking compassionate, reliable adults to become Independent Visitors - volunteer mentors and trusted friends to children and young people in care.

What is an Independent Visitor?

An Independent Visitor (IV) is a volunteer befriender and mentor who visits a young person in care once a month, usually on weekends, to enjoy fun, supportive activities together. As an IV, you’ll be a consistent, caring adult outside their professional network - someone who chooses to be there, just for them.

This is a long-term role, and we ask volunteers to commit to at least two years to help build a strong, stable relationship.

We’re especially keen to hear from volunteers based in or near London, Croydon and Kent, where many of our young people live.

Why it matters

Young people in care often face instability and frequent change. Having a consistent adult who listens, encourages and simply spends time with them can be life changing.

“My IV is the one person who’s always there for me. They make me feel like I matter.” Young Person in Care.

Who can volunteer?

You don’t need previous experience - just the right values and commitment. We’re looking for caring people who are:

  • Friendly and approachable
  • Patient, empathetic and consistent
  • A good listener
  • Committed to visiting once a month for at least two years
  • Willing to complete training and safeguarding checks

We particularly welcome applications from male volunteers and individuals from Black, Asian and other underrepresented communities.

What will you be doing?

As an Independent Visitor, you’ll:

  • Meet your young person once a month for activities like going to the cinema, bowling, exploring parks or just having a chat
  • Suggest age-appropriate outings based on their interests
  • Keep in touch between visits with a weekly call or message (if they’d like)
  • Occasionally join in on group events
  • Create meaningful, lasting memories

Please note that all travel and activity expenses will be covered.

Training & ongoing support

Before you start, we’ll provide:

  • Full initial training
  • Ongoing support and one-to-one supervision
  • Access to additional training through Southwark’s volunteer resources

Contact information

  • For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Sav D’Souza via email at .uk

Recruitment timeline

  • Applications reviewed on an ongoing basis.
  • Interviews: To be confirmed.

The closing date is given as a guide. We reserve the right to close this vacancy once a sufficient number of applications has been received. We strongly advise you to complete your application as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

Ready to make a difference?

If you’re looking for a rewarding, long-term volunteering opportunity where you can support a young person one to one and help them thrive, we’d love to receive an application from you today!

Additional Information

Southwark Council will only contact candidates through official Council recruitment channels. We will not ask you to provide passport details, proof of address, National Insurance number, bank details or payment at application stage. These checks are only requested at the onboarding process – once an offer of employment has been made. If you’re unsure whether a communication you’ve received is genuine, please contact the Resourcing team directly on .uk before sharing any personal information.

About the Content Coordinator

Stories have the power to change lives. As our Content and Engagement Coordinator, you will help ensure that the experiences of missing people, families and those who support them are heard, understood and inspire action.


This is a varied and creative role at the heart of our Fundraising and Communications team. You will work across the charity to identify powerful stories, build meaningful relationships with people who want to share their experiences, and transform those experiences into compelling content across social media, our website, campaigns and fundraising activity. Working closely with colleagues from services, policy, communications and fundraising, you will help bring the impact of Missing People and SafeCall to life in ways that engage audiences, build support and strengthen our influence.


You will be equally comfortable planning content, interviewing contributors, creating engaging digital content, coordinating volunteers and spotting opportunities to amplify our message. Above all, you will understand that behind every story is a person, and will approach your work with creativity, empathy and sensitivity.


The impact you will have

Every year, thousands of people go missing and countless families are left searching for answers. The stories you uncover and share will help people understand the realities of missing, raise awareness of the support available, and inspire others to take action.


By developing and amplifying lived-experience stories, you will help strengthen fundraising campaigns, increase engagement across our digital channels, support influencing and policy work, and demonstrate the life-changing impact of our services. Your work will ensure that the voices of missing people and their families remain at the centre of everything we do.


The content you create will help more people find support when they need it, encourage communities to engage with our mission, and build greater understanding of the issues surrounding missing. In doing so, you will play an important role in advancing our vision of a future where every missing person is safe.


About you

You will be highly organised, enjoy working with systems and data, and take pride in delivering accurate, high-quality work. You will find full details of what we are looking for in the attached job description. As well as having the right to work in the UK for 28 hours per week, the key requirements are:


Experience:

  • Creating engaging content for a range of digital and offline channels, including social media, websites, email and campaigns.

  • Identifying, developing and producing impactful case studies, interviews or lived-experience stories.

  • Building positive working relationships with a range of stakeholders and managing competing priorities.

  • Planning content and managing multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.

  • Using content performance data and audience insights to inform recommendations and improve content.

  • Writing for SEO, AIO GEO and AEO and user experienced informed website content.

  • Creating multimedia content, including photography, video or audio.

  • Supporting integrated campaigns involving fundraising, communications, policy or service delivery teams.


Skills and Knowledge:

  • Knowledge of SEO, GEO and emerging search practices, including AI-generated search experiences.

  • Exceptional written communication skills, with the ability to adapt tone and style for different audiences.

  • Strong interviewing and story-gathering skills, with the ability to build trust and help people share their experiences confidently.

  • Ability to identify compelling stories and translate complex information into clear, engaging and accessible content.

  • Understanding of content planning and how content can be adapted effectively across multiple channels.

  • Good understanding of social media platforms, audience engagement and content best practice.

  • Confidence using digital content management systems and common marketing tools.

  • Ability to motivate, enthuse and inspire others, including direct reports and volunteers;

  • Ability to develop and drive forward new projects and initiatives, taking the lead and/or working collaboratively with colleagues;


Plus:

Basic criminal record check will be completed upon appointment and must be deemed satisfactory by Missing People before the start date.


What you will get in return

Missing People is a friendly and supportive place to work – it’s a welcoming, caring organisation which really makes a difference to people affected by the issue of missing throughout the UK. We offer generous paid holidays, a range of enhanced family friendly benefits and are happy to talk about flexible working in most roles.

Youth Engagement Mentor

Location: Manchester & Surrounding Areas

Pay Rate: £25.00 - £30.00 per hour

Contract: Flexible / Student-Centred

The Mission: Building a Bridge to the Future

Many young people today feel forgotten by the traditional education system. As a Youth Engagement Mentor, you aren't just a tutor; you are a lifeline. You will work one-on-one with students who are persistently absent or excluded from school, including those with SEND, SEMH challenges, or complex barriers to learning.

Your mission is to build a "re-engagement bridge," guiding students from total isolation back into a stable learning environment, college, or vocational pathway.

The Role: Impact Beyond the Classroom

Your daily "to-do" list is rarely linear. You will focus on three pillars: Stability, Skill-building, and Advocacy.

  • Relationship Building & Wellbeing: Meet the young person where they are-sometimes literally at their front door-to build trust. You will deliver 1:1 sessions focused on confidence, emotional regulation, and self-esteem, providing a calm, trauma-informed presence during moments of crisis.

  • Educational & Vocational Re-ignition: Deliver low-pressure, interest-based activities to reignite the habit of learning. You will physically accompany students to interviews or placements to reduce anxiety and teach vital life skills like budgeting and navigating public transport.

  • Collaboration & Advocacy: Act as the "voice of the child" in multi-agency meetings with Social Care and CAMHS. You will also support parents in creating a home environment that encourages attendance and growth.

Who We Are Looking ForWhy This Role Matters

"Many of these young people have been told they are 'failures' by the system. Your job isn't to force them into a classroom; it's to prove to them that they are capable of success, regardless of what a traditional school setting says."

You’ll also support our growth activity through outreach calls, helping us stay connected with potential clients and maintain a healthy pipeline.

You’ll also advise leaders with calm confidence, simplify complexity, and move businesses forward with thoughtful, commercially sound HR. Protecting scope and planning your time with discipline is essential to how we keep our promises.

Health – We create space to think, breathe and work sustainably.
Equity – We bring clarity, consistency and compassion to every decision.
Responsibility – We own our work and show up with integrity.
Optimism – We believe in people’s potential and help them move forward.
Innovation – We design thoughtful solutions, not templates.
Courage – We say the hard things with warmth and honesty.


What You’ll Do

  • Build early connections with future clients through daily outreach calls

  • Support organisational change with calm, clear thinking

  • Use insight and data to demonstrate impact

  • Plan and track your time with discipline so clients receive the service they’ve purchased


Who You Are

You'll thrive here if you:

  • Enjoy variety and can move between clients with clarity and calm

  • Communicate with warmth, honesty and belief in others

  • Bring strong commercial judgement and protect scope without drama

  • Are organised, proactive and confident managing a high-volume workflow

  • Are curious, reflective and committed to your own development

Jollyes are an award-winning UK pet retailer with over 100 stores and over 50 years of pet expertise between our paws. Our client is seeking a highly organised, proactive and detail-oriented Buying Administrator to join their busy Buying Department.

1. Buying & Purchasing Administration

  • Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Buying Team.

  • Maintain records and update internal systems.
  • Assist with pricing updates, cost calculations and product margin information.

  • Liaise with all suppliers regarding product information, pricing, samples and order updates.
  • Request and collate supplier quotations, specifications and relevant documentation.
  • Maintain accurate supplier contact details and product records.
  • Follow up on outstanding information to ensure buying deadlines are achieved.
  • Assist in resolving discrepancies relating to orders, costs, deliveries and product specifications.

  • Support the Buying Team with the introduction and development of new product ranges.
  • Assist in sourcing and coordinating product samples for review and approval.
  • Maintain accurate product specifications, including dimensions, materials, colours, packaging and other relevant information.
  • Coordinate product photography, descriptions and technical information for catalogues, websites and sales materials.
  • Assist with product range reviews, seasonal launches and new product presentations.
  • Ensure product information is accurate, complete and available within agreed deadlines.

4. Stock & Delivery Coordination

  • Work closely with the Buying, Sales and Warehouse Teams to support product availability.
  • Monitor expected delivery dates and communicate changes to relevant departments.
  • Support the management of discontinued products, overstocks and seasonal stock transitions.
  • Help maintain accurate stock and incoming shipment information.

5. Data Management & Reporting

  • Create and maintain product records within the company's internal systems.
  • Ensure product codes, descriptions, costs, selling prices and supplier details are accurately recorded.
  • Prepare and maintain Excel spreadsheets.
  • Assist with sales analysis, stock performance reports and product range reviews.
  • Maintain organised electronic filing systems and documentation.
  • Ensure confidentiality and accuracy when handling commercially sensitive information.

  • Assist in preparing product information for seasonal catalogues across a variety of ranges.
  • Work with the Marketing and Sales Teams to ensure accurate product descriptions, specifications and pricing.
  • Support the coordination of product samples for photography, trade shows and customer presentations.
  • Help ensure new product launches and seasonal buying deadlines are achieved.
  • Assist in maintaining product information throughout the lifecycle of each range.

Skills & Experience

Essential:

  • Previous experience in an administrative role, ideally within buying, purchasing, merchandising or wholesale.
  • Excellent organisational skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritise workloads and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • Confident working with numerical information, spreadsheets and product data.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • A proactive and flexible approach to problem-solving.
  • Ability to work accurately under pressure and meet deadlines.

Desirable:

  • Previous experience within a seasonal buying or purchasing department.
  • Experience working with overseas suppliers, particularly Far Eastern manufacturers.
  • Knowledge of import purchasing procedures and international shipping.
  • Experience within the home, garden, seasonal decorations or general merchandise sectors.
  • Familiarity with stock management, purchasing or ERP systems.
  • Experience supporting product development, catalogue production or seasonal range launches.
  • Understanding of product costing, margins and retail pricing.

Personal Attributes

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • Attention to Detail: A methodical approach with a high level of accuracy.
  • Organisation: The ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Communication: Confidence in dealing with suppliers and colleagues across different departments.
  • Teamwork: A collaborative attitude and willingness to support colleagues.

  • Adaptability: Flexibility to respond to changing priorities within a seasonal business.
  • Commercial Awareness: An interest in products, pricing, purchasing and market trends.
  • Reliability: A dependable and professional approach to responsibilities.
